questions.prompt: Complete: "Nobody in the family took the ___ the specialist had given them."
questions.explanation: After "the" the sentence needs a noun, and the noun is "advice", spelt with a c. "Advise", spelt with an s, is the verb — you advise somebody to do something — and neither its -s form nor its -ing form gives the ordinary noun this sentence needs.

questions.prompt: Complete: "My cousins ___ in Sousse since their father found work there."
questions.explanation: "Since" names the point where the situation started, and a situation that started in the past and is still true today takes the present perfect: have lived. The past simple would cut the link with the present, and neither the present simple nor the present continuous can express a situation that runs from that starting point up to now.

questions.prompt: The head teacher said on Monday: "We will decide tomorrow." In the reported sentence, "tomorrow" becomes…
questions.explanation: Reporting after a past verb pushes the time words away from the moment of speaking: tomorrow becomes the next day or the following day. Leaving tomorrow untouched points at the day after the report instead of the day after the words were spoken, the day before moves in the opposite direction, and that day is what today becomes, not tomorrow.

questions.prompt: Which prefix turns "legal" into its opposite?
questions.explanation: The negative prefix takes the form "il-" in front of a word beginning with l: illegal, illiterate, illogical. "Im-" is the form used before m, p and b (impossible, impatient); "un-" and "dis-" attach to plenty of other words (unfair, disobedient) but never produce "unlegal" or "dislegal".

questions.prompt: Your partner writes the letter "S" of the correction code above the word "wich" in your draft. What must you correct?
questions.explanation: In the correction code S stands for a spelling mistake, and "wich" is the word "which" with a letter missing — a mistake inside the word. V would mean you had chosen a word that does not exist or does not fit the meaning, W.O. that the words were in the wrong order, and P that a punctuation mark was wrong.
